<teammate-message teammate_id="chirp-web-validate" color="purple" summary="Chirp web re-pinned, builds, runs, validated with Playwright">
Done. PR: https://github.com/pablof7z/chirp/pull/59 (branch chirp-web-validate, worktree /Users/pablofernandez/Work/chirp/.wt-web). Closes chirp#16.

npm install: RESOLVES cleanly against the public registry. Note the scope mismatch you flagged was real — renamed @nmp/runtime-web -> @nmpis/runtime-web and @nmp/components-web -> @nmpis/components-web (^1.0.0-rc.1) in apps/web/package.json, dropped the dead tsconfig.json `paths` mapping to nonexistent ../packages/*, and moved several deep `@nmp/components-web/src/user-avatar/{ProfileWire,NostrProfileHost,NostrAvatar}` reach-through imports onto the package's actual public `./user-avatar` subpath export (confirmed via npm pack that all three re-export from there).

Build: PASSES (tsc --noEmit && vite build), plus typecheck, typecheck:e2e, and unit tests (7/7) all green.

Run: YES, validated with Playwright in a real browser (screenshots in docs/validation/web/, committed on the branch):
1. First-run onboarding renders correctly.
2. Signed in with a memory-only local-key session (pasted nsec) — WASM worker started, 2/2 relays connected to relay.primal.net, signer accepted.
3. Composer accepts input.
4. Publish attempt correctly fails *closed* with a Rust-owned diagnostic ("pre-signed publish target rejected: requires an explicit non-empty imported/protocol relay target") rather than crashing — proves the dispatch/signing/relay path is wired end-to-end even though this fresh throwaway key had no relay list to resolve against. Didn't chase this further since it's orthogonal to the re-pin (pre-existing app relay-target-resolution behavior, not a regression from the version bump) — flagging in case you want it looked at separately.

Important gap I found and fixed beyond the re-pin: the production `vite build` reported success but was silently broken. Vite copies @nmpis/runtime-web's wasm-loader JS into dist/assets/ verbatim (it's only reached through a runtime-computed import()), but never follows THAT module's own internal `new URL(...)` references — so the actual wasm binary and SQLite vendor snippets never landed in dist/. A real prod build would fetch the wasm, silently get the SPA index.html back instead (200 OK, wrong content-type), and hang forever on "Connecting" — confirmed this with a `vite preview` + Playwright screenshot before/after. Fixed with a `closeBundle` plugin in vite.config.ts that stages the package's dist/wasm/ tree into dist/assets/ post-build; re-verified with preview+Playwright that it now reaches "connected" same as dev.

Also found apps/web/vercel.json, scripts/build.sh, and the build:wasm/build:vercel npm scripts still assumed the pre-split monorepo layout (crates/nmp-browser-runtime, pkg/nmp-browser-runtime, a root web/ workspace) that doesn't exist in the split chirp repo — that pipeline was dead on arrival for any real Vercel deploy, unrelated to my change. Removed the dead script + npm scripts, repointed vercel.json at the working `npm install` + `npm run build` path, and updated docs/chirp-web.md's Production Deployment Contract to describe the packages-based reality instead of the stale monorepo-source-build contract. This is consumer-repo work so I fixed it directly rather than filing it.

No NMP framework issues needed — everything blocking a real run was fixable in Chirp. Bottom line: Chirp web now genuinely works end-to-end (dev and real production build) against the published NMP packages.
</teammate-message>
